objective: Al terminar expresas arrepentimiento y situaciones pasadas imaginarias con el tercer condicional (if + past perfect, would have + participio).

warmup.prompt_es: 'Si hubiera sabido, habría venido.' El tercer condicional habla de un pasado que no ocurrió y de sus consecuencias imaginarias. Sirve para lamentar, criticar y deducir.

text: When I look back on my career, there are things I would do differently. If I had known how competitive the job market was, I would have started applying earlier. I didn't, so I missed several opportunities. If I hadn't been so shy in interviews, I might have got the position at the bank. And if I had taken that internship in Paris, I would probably have learned French much faster.

Still, not everything was a mistake. If I hadn't left my first company, I wouldn't have met my current boss. If she hadn't believed in me, I wouldn't have been promoted so quickly. And if I had stayed in my home town, I would never have discovered how much I enjoy managing people.

Would I have been happier if I had chosen a different path? Perhaps. But I wouldn't have learned what I know today. As my mentor once said, 'If you hadn't made those mistakes, you wouldn't be the person you are now.'
input.es: Cuando miro atrás en mi carrera, hay cosas que haría de otra manera. Si hubiera sabido lo competitivo que era el mercado laboral, habría empezado a presentar candidaturas antes. No lo hice y perdí varias oportunidades. Si no hubiera sido tan tímido en las entrevistas, quizá habría conseguido el puesto en el banco. Y si hubiera aceptado aquellas prácticas en París, probablemente habría aprendido francés mucho más rápido. Aun así, no todo fue un error. Si no hubiera dejado mi primera empresa, no habría conocido a mi jefa actual. Si ella no hubiera creído en mí, no me habrían ascendido tan rápido. Y si me hubiera quedado en mi ciudad, nunca habría descubierto cuánto me gusta dirigir personas. ¿Habría sido más feliz si hubiera elegido otro camino? Quizá. Pero no habría aprendido lo que sé hoy. Como dijo una vez mi mentor: 'Si no hubieras cometido esos errores, no serías la persona que eres ahora'.

md_es: | *if + past perfect* | *would (not) have + participio* | *If I **had known**, I **would have come**.* |
| *if + past perfect* | *could have / might have + participio* | *If she **hadn't been** late, she **might have got** the job.* |
**Uso:** hechos pasados que **no ocurrieron** (lo contrario de la realidad). Sirve para lamentar, reprochar o deducir.
- Realidad: *I didn't study, so I failed.* → Imaginario: *If I had studied, I wouldn't have failed.*
- *would have* = certeza imaginaria · *could have* = posibilidad/capacidad · *might have* = posibilidad menos segura.
- Pregunta: *What would you have done if you had been in my position?* · *Would she have accepted if you had asked?*
**Inversión formal (sin if):** *Had I known, I would have called.* · *Had she not left, …* (muy formal; se ve en B2 avanzado).
**Contracciones:** *I'd have come = I would have come* y *If I'd known = If I had known*. Atención: *'d* es *had* tras *if* y *would* en la principal.
- ✘ *If I would have known, …* → ✔ *If I had known, …* (nunca *would* en la cláusula if).
- ✘ *If I had known, I would come.* → ✔ *… I would have come.*
- ✘ *If I knew, I would have come.* → ✔ *If I had known, I would have come.*
**Ojo:** en lenguaje informal oirás *If I would have known* (americano coloquial) pero en exámenes es incorrecto.
Pronunciación: *would have* /ˈwʊd əv/ (se escucha 'would of'; se escribe *would have*) · *hadn't been* /ˈhædnt biːn/ · *might have* /ˈmaɪt əv/.

common_mistakes_es.wrong: If I had known, I would come.
common_mistakes_es.right: If I had known, I would have come.
